🔄 QRP-Auto Mode

For weak QRP signals and patient operation. While active, the busy lock is enforced (never transmit on a busy channel). When the frequency is clear, the app connects to the gateway by itself — repeated at the chosen interval, until the transfer completes cleanly (connection established and properly closed) or the maximum duration is reached. Requires: callsign + target gateway set, TRX connected.

Radio & Connection
TRX frequency: —
RX level — calibration
– CLIP
8-bit audio over CAT: peaks belong in the green band (40–80 %). Too low throws away real resolution, CLIP destroys the decode. Set the level on the radio (AF / volume) — digital gain does not help.
Audio devices (Android: pick the radio, not the mic)
On Android the browser defaults to the phone's built-in microphone, so receive audio never reaches the decoder (the level jumps when you breathe on the phone). If that happens, pick the radio's USB sound card here for both input and output. Empty labels are normal before the first connect — connect once, then choose. The choice is remembered.
Test tone (tune / modulation check)
Keys the transmitter and sends a steady 1 kHz tone for 5 s at reduced power, over the same USB audio path as ARDOP — so it checks the tuner/PA and the modulation at once. ⚠ This transmits on your dial frequency: make sure it is clear and legal for you. A carrier stresses the PA thermally — run QRP rigs (tr)uSDX/QMX only briefly. Stops automatically after 5 s.

Language
4FSK demodulator
SDFT tolerates sample-rate drift much better and is preset for the (tr)uSDX (whose sound card drifts). For TRX with a precise sound card (Icom, QMX) the more efficient Goertzel demodulator is preset. Reset to the matching default on every TRX selection; switch here if you have decode problems or unusual propagation conditions.

Decoder / Protocol
ARDOP Winlink by DL2MAN
This project stands on the shoulders of others. Our heartfelt thanks to everyone whose work made this client possible — Rick Muething (KN6KB) and the ardopcf team for ARDOP, Martin Hebnes Pedersen (LA5NTA) for wl2k-go, F6FBB for the forwarding protocol, Haruyasu Yoshizaki for LZHUF, the ARSFI for the Winlink network, and Guido (PE1NNZ) for the (tr)uSDX.
A complete ARDOP modem stack and Winlink client (B2F) running entirely in the browser — for QRP operation with (tr)uSDX, IC-705, IC-7300 and QMX. Project lead, protocol and architecture decisions, hardware and OTA testing: Manuel, DL2MAN. Implementation and programming: Claude (Anthropic).
Sources & Protocols Used

ARDOP — Amateur Radio Digital Open Protocol
Protocol specification and original implementation: Rick Muething, KN6KB.

ardopcf — C reference implementation of ARDOP, from which the modem and protocol stack was ported 1:1.
© 2014–2024 Rick Muething (KN6KB), John Wiseman (G8BPQ), Peter LaRue (AI7YN) · MIT license
github.com/pflarue/ardop

wl2k-go — Winlink framework for Go; reference for the B2F layer and LZHUF compression.
© 2014–2016 Martin Hebnes Pedersen (LA5NTA) · MIT license
github.com/la5nta/wl2k-go

B2F / FBB forwarding protocol
FBB protocol: Jean-Paul Roubelat, F6FBB. B2F reference implementation: paclink-unix (Nicholas S. Castellano, N2QZ, and others).

LZHUF compression
Original algorithm and code: Haruyasu Yoshizaki (1988). Maintained implementation: the JNOS developers.

Winlink / WL2K
The Winlink 2000 network is a project of the Amateur Radio Safety Foundation, Inc. (ARSFI).

CAT control
Icom CI-V command reference (IC-7300, IC-705) — © Icom Inc. (tr)uSDX and QMX are controlled via Kenwood-compatible CAT commands (TS-480).

Winlink gateway list
RMS channel list (ARDOP) from winlink.org/RMSChannels — ARSFI. Winlink Web Services API (api.winlink.org) as a research source for the update feature.

(tr)uSDX — target platform / transceiver.
DL2MAN (Manuel) and Guido, PE1NNZ.
